purpose: Purpose-built language-model accelerator hardware with unusually large on-card memory and low claimed board power. Vendor capacity and performance claims are retained with explicit provenance and are not treated as independent benchmarks.

hardware.architecture: Six HTX301 Language Processing Unit (LPU) chips using Skymizer LISA v3; decode-first design with prefill/decode disaggregation
hardware.memory_type: standard LPDDR-class; Skymizer HyperThought material references LPDDR4/LPDDR5
hardware.host_interface: PCIe card; exact PCIe generation and lane width not publicly specified
hardware.form_factor: single PCIe accelerator card / evaluation board; exact dimensions, slot width and auxiliary-power connectors not publicly specified
hardware.cooling: not publicly specified; complete chassis airflow requirements remain to be verified
hardware.model_reach_vendor_claim: 4B to 700B parameters on the six-chip HTX301 reference card
software: Skymizer proprietary LPU orchestration for prefill/decode disaggregation

vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.claim: HTX301 six-chip PCIe reference card supports up to 700B-parameter LLM inference with 384GB on-card memory at approximately 240W
vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.evidence_scope: manufacturer product page and launch announcement
vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.normalization_caveat: No independent benchmark, model identity, quantization, context length, prefill/decode rate or end-to-end host power is published for the 700B claim.

vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.claim: HyperThought octa-core HTX301 processor reaches 240 tokens/s for Llama 2 7B prefill; multi-chip HyperThought scales to 1200 tokens/s for Llama 7B prefill
vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.normalization_caveat: These are platform-level prefill claims and should not be interpreted as verified six-chip-card decode throughput.

vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.claim: HyperThought efficiency point of 30 tokens/s at 100GB/s memory bandwidth and 0.5 TOPS
vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.normalization_caveat: The vendor does not identify this as the six-chip HTX301 card configuration, so it is retained only as architecture-level evidence.

hardware.quantization_compatibility: Skymizer states HyperThought can execute multiple quantized LLMs and uses proprietary weight and KV-cache compression. Public material does not specify drop-in GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ, EXL2, FP8, INT8 or INT4 file compatibility, so those formats must not be assumed. Deployment uses Skymizer's compiler/runtime path.

llm_suitability.practical_guidance: 384GB of on-card memory is enough capacity for many very large quantized models and is marketed for models through 700B, but practical tokens/s cannot be inferred without memory-bandwidth, quantization, context and decode measurements. Treat the current platform as an early-access inference appliance/reference card rather than a general CUDA/ROCm replacement.

hardware.off_grid_suitability: low_to_moderate_for_card_level_capacity; approximately 240W board power is unusually low for the claimed memory/model capacity, but a host system and unknown cooling overhead are required
hardware.efficiency_notes: 384GB / ~240W gives a simple specification-derived capacity ratio of about 1.6GB of on-card memory per board watt. This is not tokens/joule and does not include host, cooling or power-supply losses.
hardware.cost_efficiency: unknown_quote_only; no defensible public numeric card price was verified

pricing.note: Skymizer offers an early-access/request-preview form but no public card MSRP or distributor street price.

source_caveats: The HTX301 product page states 4B-700B reach for the six-chip reference card, while the broader HyperThought platform page currently states model reach up to 600B. This record uses the product-specific 700B claim and preserves the discrepancy.
Skymizer says figures reflect the HTX301 reference platform and are subject to change ahead of general availability.

The exact on-card LPDDR generation/mix, aggregate memory bandwidth, PCIe generation/lanes, card dimensions, cooling requirement, power connectors, supported model formats and independent token-generation performance are not publicly specified.
The product is early access, not verified broadly retail-available hardware.
